reason: The text explicitly names Rahab (רָחָב), described as a woman and prostitute/innkeeper (אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה). She functions as a helper and ally to the Israelite spies, but does not hold a leadership position. Therefore, not all named characters in the passage are leaders.
